recipes.name: Habanero Hot Sauce
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Heat oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add carrots, onion, and garlic; cook and stir until onion is translucent, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat.
Transfer vegetables to a blender. Add habanero peppers, tomato, water, lime juice, and vinegar; blend until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Transfer mixture to a saucepan and simmer over medium-low heat until a bit thicker, about 3 to 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Habanero Hot Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This habanero hot sauce recipe is a blend of habanero peppers, tomato, garlic, lime, and vinegar for a fiery addition to tacos, mayo, or anything!

review.reviewBody: The recipe has 2 measurements backwards: 1. Carrots should be 1 Cup (not 1 tablespoon) 2. Water should be 1 Tablespoon - give or take (not 1 Cup) That should help out considerably. Add Habaneros as desired!!!

After reading about the tomato issue I dropped it but I replaced it with a good sized ripe mango, 'bout the size of my hand and most likely if using frozen chunked I'd say a cup. I zested the lime and added it to the mix too. Used apple cider vinegar instead of white, dropped the carrots because I'd totally forgotten about them actually so that's probably why the mango worked well. 
I used 7 small peppers but I deseeded 4 of them, I still had plenty of heat. Added 1/2 teaspoon Not smoked paprika and about 1/4 teaspoon of Demerara sugar.
I made this as a gift for a friend that "collects hot sauce" and it was a major hit at the party. Everybody loved it! My hubby heard someone joking "this hot sauce is like Jodi, sweet and smooth then comes up behind you and kicks you in the head" I also got a "velvet brick" comment. 
Oh! like other reviewers I used Only One Tbl of water not the 1/4 cup! I also put my chopped peppers in a steamer and steamed for 5 minutes And without adding water I tossed my chopped mango in the microwave covered for 3 minutes to maximize their flavor. I put my paprika with my onions when I sweated them to wake up the paprika flavor and remove that "raw" spice flavor from it. Winner recipe and btw, this made a perfect pint sized jar full.

I added 1/2 cup lime, and less water, more chilli, carrot, onion tomato , 1/2 cup apple cider vinegar, lots more garlic and 1tblspn raw sugar, 1 tblspn pink salt. Used a hand blender in the pot and pulsed till smooth then simmered for 10 minutes. Turned out nice and spicy. Will mature very well I think.

I have made this recipe a few times and its a big hit at dinner parties. I make the "Tex Mex Pork" from Allrecipes and put the shredded pork in its sauce over pasta and add the "Habanero Hot Sauce" with sour cream as a condiment and everyone loves the combination! The only modification I make to this recipe is I cut open my habanero and remove the seeds and stem. My husband and I love hot food, but we managed to ruin a different recipe when we added whole habaneros because it was so hot that we couldn't eat the stew we had slaved over for an entire afternoon. I opt to put my habaneros in a pyrex and steam the habaneros in a double boiler for about 7 minutes. I think this mellows out the hotness of the sauce without losing any flavor. I add everything to a food processor minus the tomato and it makes a delicious fairly spicy sauce that pleases the masses.

I seeded the habaneros and used about 8 of them. I also just used a stick blender and blended the mixture in the pot. With the seeds removed, the sauce has great flavour and only moderate heat. Definitely a keeper

I've made this a few times and people love it. I've made a few changes. I use at least double the habanero peppers. I half the tomato or less per batch. I also add a few fresh cayenne and a couple tablespoons of crushed fresh paprika peppers.
Also once I soften the carrot etc I combine the rest into the pot and cook for a minute or so...I use an immersion blender which takes awhile but the result is amazing.
Added cumin, more lime, a whole red pepper, 2 tablespoons of sugar, more vinegar, more garlic, and only a 1/4 of a tomato. Cook veggies longer and simmer final product for 15 minutes, covered.

I double the recipe and used my instant pot to cook this up. I didn't sauté anything. I just chopped it up and threw it in the instant pot. I cooked on high for 15 minutes. I then put it in the blender until smooth. I did add a handful of sugar to balance it out.

I doubled recipe & tripled the chilies and I used a couple of shallots instead of the onions. I used rice vinegar, since I had it & mixed everything up in the food processor (so no need to pre-cook the carrots) and then cooked it in a saucepan, as directed. I put it into sterilized canning jars - one for now, one for later. Yum! The flavor of the carrots & chilies is perfect. A friend who makes sauces like this all the time suggests letting the sauce 'cure' for a time before using.

I made this going by the 4x directions in one pot with an immersion blender. Definitely a mild sauce for slathering on burritos or something, and chunky when made with an immersion blender, that could be used as a salsa. Might make a good "hot" sauce with three times the peppers.

Made 2 batches. In both, added apple cider vinegar in addition to white vinegar thus doubling the amount of vinegar. Also, added 1/4 cup of molasses, paprika, a total of 15 habanero peppers And Dijon mustard to both. I did add one can of tomato paste to the second batch only. Both came out great flavor and excellent heat. The batch with paste had a mildly less intense heat and a sweeter note. Love then both.
Very good and long lasting heat in this one. Good flavor and good base to add maybe some blueberries or peaches to the mix.
Great taste! I used some Ghost Peppers for this one but again I’ll make a larger batch and can it.

Had to use a food processor instead of a blender. Was worried that the chunky salsa-like consistency that resulted would distract from its purpose, so I put it through a sieve. Very content with the results.
Added a few more peppers for an extra kick but it’s delicious.
Good balanced flavor. Didn't add seeds so it was not very hot. A nice spice though. Easy to eat with chips and not need milk or something to put the fire out. Easy recipe and will be using it again.
Next time I will add a little cumin.
This sauce is excellent , I added a cup of fresh cilantro that knocked it out of the park
Doubled up the habaneros in the recipe, Awesome sauce!!!!
i made this, except i put in 10 habaneros and as it was not spicy enough. (it tastes like Nando's extra spicy piri piri sauce)
